'''Edna Ernestine Kramer Lassar''' (May 11, 1902 &ndash; July 9, 1984), born '''Edna Ernestine Kramer''', was an American [[mathematician]] and author of mathematics books.

Kramer was born in [[Manhattan]] to Jewish immigrants.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/kramer.htm|title=Edna Kramer Lassar|website=Biographies of Women Mathematicians|publisher=Agnes Scott College|date=May 1997}}</ref> She earned her [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] ''summa cum laude'' in mathematics from [[Hunter College]] in 1922.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov/lccn/sn83030193/1922-06-15/ed-1/seq-26/|title=The evening world. (New York, N.Y.) 1887-1931, June 15, 1922, Wall Street Final Edition, Image 26|journal=The Evening World|date=1922-06-15|access-date=2017-10-20|pages=26|issn=1941-0654}}</ref> While teaching at local high schools, she earned her [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] in 1925 and [[Ph.D.]] in 1930 in mathematics (with a minor in physics) from [[Columbia University]] with [[Edward Kasner]] as her advisor.

She wrote ''The Nature and Growth of Modern Mathematics'', ''A First Course in Educational Statistics,'' ''Mathematics Takes Wings: An Aviation Supplement to Secondary Mathematics'', and ''The Main Stream of Mathematics''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=July 25, 1984 |title=Dr. Edna Kramer-Lassar, 82, Ex-Professor of Mathematics |url=http://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1984/07/25/087253.html?pageNumber=94 |access-date=2022-04-09 |website=The New York Times |page=D23 |language=en}}</ref>

Kramer married the French teacher Benedict Taxier Lassar on July 2, 1935. Kramer-Lassar died at the age of 82 in [[Manhattan]] of [[Parkinson's disease]].<ref name=":0" />

== Works ==
* ''The Main Stream of Mathematics'' {{sic}} (1951)
* ''The Nature and Growth of Modern Mathematics'' (1970)
